raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation `ForwardBatch.compute_spec_mrope_positions` builds the per-step MRoPE position tensor for multimodal requests by stacking each request's `mrope_position_delta` on host and shipping it to device with `.to(device=device)`. The source (`torch.stack`'s output) is pageable, so PyTorch appends a `cudaStreamSynchronize` to that H2D copy — the driver cannot let the DMA proceed asynchronously because the OS could swap the source page mid-transfer. The host blocks until every kernel already queued on the stream has retired. This function runs every step of speculative decode (both target verify and draft extend call it), so the queued work behind the sync is the whole in-flight draft/verify window. On an MTP (NEXTN) deployment (TP8), this turned an 8-byte copy into a multi-millisecond stall per call — profiling showed two such stalls per decode step (~1.4ms and ~7.7ms), each draining the stream and then starving the GPU while the host re-issued kernels one at a time instead of running ahead on a primed queue. ## Modifications Stage the stacked delta tensor through pinned host memory before the H2D, so `non_blocking=True` actually applies (it only takes effect when the source is pinned): ```python stacked = torch.stack(deltas, dim=0) if stacked.device.type != "cpu" or not is_pin_memory_available(device): return stacked.to(device=device) staging = torch.empty(stacked.shape, dtype=stacked.dtype, pin_memory=True) staging.copy_(stacked) return staging.to(device=device, non_blocking=True) ``` CUDA's per-stream ordering still guarantees the copy completes before any kernel that reads `mrope_delta_tensor` executes — only the host-side wait is removed. - Falls back to the original blocking `.to(device=device)` when `is_pin_memory_available(device)` is `False` (CPU-only / unsupported accelerators), so no behavior change there. - Value, dtype, device and shape of the result are unchanged. - Extra host allocation is a `[batch_size, 1]` int64 tensor per step (a few hundred bytes); PyTorch's caching host allocator reuses the pinned block across steps, so there's no unbounded pinned-memory growth. - Does not touch the text-only fast path (batch has no multimodal requests), which already returns before this tensor is built. - No new env var / flag — this always applies when pinned memory is available, matching how `non_blocking=True` H2D is already handled elsewhere in this file (e.g. `_compute_mrope_positions_decode`). ## Accuracy Tests This change only replaces how the host→device transfer is performed; the value, dtype, device and shape of `mrope_delta_tensor` are identical to before. `test_spec_mrope_positions_graph` in `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_next_verify_prep.py` already calls `compute_spec_mrope_positions` end to end with `mixed=True` (the exact branch this PR touches) and asserts the output against a reference computation, under both eager and CUDA-graph replay. That test passes unmodified against this change, which is expected since the output values are unaffected. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on an MTP (NEXTN) deployment, TP8, Qwen3.5-VL-class model, `livingroom_planner` multimodal workload, steady-state decode: | Metric | Before | After | Change | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Per-step GPU utilization (busy time summed across all CUDA streams used by draft/verify/draft-extend) | 65.6% | 81.2% | **+15.6 pp** | | `scheduler.run_batch` wall time (median) | 20375 us | 17630 us | **-13.5%** | | Blocking `cudaStreamSynchronize` time inside one decode step | 9119 us | 5517 us | **-3602 us** | The two target stalls (`[[1,1],[1,1]]`-shaped pageable H2D copies inside target-verify and draft-extend, ~1.4ms and ~7.7ms respectively) no longer appear in the trace after this change. Standalone microbenchmark isolating the function under real queued GPU work (enqueue ~240 small matmuls on the stream, then call the function): | Path | Host-side call time | |---|---:| | Original (pageable, blocking) | ~250 ms | | This PR (pinned, non_blocking) | ~0.2 ms | before: after: Measured TPOT improved by 11% on A800 (4.51 ms → 4.07 ms) and by 35% on B300 (2.38 ms → 1.76 ms). ## Verified **Internal (MTP/NEXTN, TP8, Qwen3.5-VL-class):** per-step GPU utilization (busy time summed across all CUDA streams) rose from 65.6% to 81.2%; scheduler `run_batch` wall time down 13.5%. **Third-party, end-to-end (by @esarafian, on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next / NEXTN MTP):** - *Exactness, GB300 (deterministic):* 12 image + 8 text-only greedy requests → byte-identical outputs vs main; each tree self-reproduces. - *Throughput, RTX PRO 6000 (TP2):* +6.2% median tok/s (962.5 vs 924.5), same accept length 2.48. - *Throughput, GB300 (TP1, A-B-B-A ablation isolating `forward_batch_info.py`):* 1003 vs 884 tok/s (+13.5%), median TPOT 14.95 vs 17.32 ms (−14%), accept length 2.42–2.44 in every run. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #40657442481](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40657442481) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #40657442840](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40657442840) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #40657442793](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40657442793) ## Acknowledgements This work was completed during my employment at Spirit AI as part of an effort to optimize speculative decoding performance in SGLang.

@hnyls2002 Could you help tag this PR with `/tag-and-rerun-ci` so CI can run? This is a small, focused change limited to `compute_spec_mrope_positions` in `forward_batch_info.py` (stage the MRoPE delta through pinned memory before the H2D copy instead of the current blocking pageable copy). Happy to address any review feedback. Thanks!

We measured this end to end on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (MRoPE VLM) with NEXTN MTP, with images in every request so each verify and draft step goes through the mixed branch you changed. Image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261103-797af717`; main `8d4e1ce4c7` vs this PR merged onto it (no conflicts).

**Exactness, GB300 (deterministic).** One GB300, TP1, public `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`:

```
--tp 1 --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --disable-radix-cache --enable-deterministic-inference --attention-backend flashinfer
```

We sent 12 greedy chat requests, each with a 448×448 image, plus 8 text-only greedy requests. Main and this PR produce identical outputs on all 20, and each tree also reproduces itself exactly.

**Throughput, RTX PRO 6000 (SM120).** 2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (300 W), TP2, public `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, same NEXTN 3/1/4, `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass --disable-radix-cache`.

```
python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name image --image-count 1 \
  --image-resolution 448x448 --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --num-prompts 96 --max-concurrency 16 --seed {1,2,3,4}
```

The order was main → PR → main, with one warm-up run per server.

| | out tok/s (seeds 1–4) | median | median TPOT | accept length |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main | 918 / 954 / 879 / 931 | 924.5 | 15.81 ms | 2.48 |
| this PR | 966 / 956 / 959 / 975 | 962.5 | 15.27 ms | 2.48 |
| main again | 937 / 880 / 894 / 888 | 891 | 16.52 ms | 2.47 |

Every PR run is above every main run: +6.2% against the median of the 8 main runs, with the same acceptance. That fits the per-step stream sync you saw in the profile.

**Throughput, GB300.** We used the same GB300 setup without deterministic mode (`--disable-radix-cache`, default attention backend) and the same image bench (seeds 1–3, warm-up first). The runs were A-B-B-A on one node, in a single allocation. "A" is this PR's tree with only `forward_batch_info.py` swapped back to main's version.

| arm | out tok/s (seeds 1–3) | median TPOT |
|---|---|---:|
| main | 861 / 857 / 888 | 17.46 / 18.03 / 16.82 ms |
| this PR | 997 / 1013 / 1014 | 14.92 / 14.97 / 14.85 ms |
| this PR | 1008 / 998 / 970 | 14.67 / 15.10 / 14.98 ms |
| main | 889 / 887 / 881 | 17.18 / 17.47 / 16.90 ms |

That is a median of 1003 vs 884 tok/s (+13.5%) and a median TPOT of 14.95 vs 17.32 ms (−14%), with accept length 2.42–2.44 in every run. The gain is larger here than in the TP2 RTX setup above. We did not isolate why (different host CPU, TP and checkpoint), but it is consistent with the multi-ms stalls in your profile.

Thanks for the thorough end-to-end validation — and especially the A-B-B-A ablation that isolates`forward_batch_info.py` . That pins the gain to exactly the change in this PR, which is the strongest possible evidence.

@@ -69,7 +69,11 @@

 )

+)
 
 if TYPE_CHECKING:
     from sglang.srt.configs.model_config import ModelConfig
@@ -1544,7 +1548,7 @@ def compute_spec_mrope_positions(
                 )
                 for i in range(batch_size)
             ]
-            mrope_delta_tensor = torch.stack(mrope_deltas, dim=0).to(device=device)

@hnyls2002 Could you help tag this PR with `/tag-and-rerun-ci` so CI can run? This is a small, focused change limited to `compute_spec_mrope_positions` in `forward_batch_info.py` (stage the MRoPE delta through pinned memory before the H2D copy instead of the current blocking pageable copy). Happy to address any review feedback. Thanks!

We measured this end to end on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (MRoPE VLM) with NEXTN MTP, with images in every request so each verify and draft step goes through the mixed branch you changed. Image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261103-797af717`; main `8d4e1ce4c7` vs this PR merged onto it (no conflicts).

**Exactness, GB300 (deterministic).** One GB300, TP1, public `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`:

```
--tp 1 --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --disable-radix-cache --enable-deterministic-inference --attention-backend flashinfer
```

We sent 12 greedy chat requests, each with a 448×448 image, plus 8 text-only greedy requests. Main and this PR produce identical outputs on all 20, and each tree also reproduces itself exactly.

**Throughput, RTX PRO 6000 (SM120).** 2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (300 W), TP2, public `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4`, same NEXTN 3/1/4, `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass --disable-radix-cache`.

```
python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name image --image-count 1 \
  --image-resolution 448x448 --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --num-prompts 96 --max-concurrency 16 --seed {1,2,3,4}
```

The order was main → PR → main, with one warm-up run per server.

| | out tok/s (seeds 1–4) | median | median TPOT | accept length |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| main | 918 / 954 / 879 / 931 | 924.5 | 15.81 ms | 2.48 |
| this PR | 966 / 956 / 959 / 975 | 962.5 | 15.27 ms | 2.48 |
| main again | 937 / 880 / 894 / 888 | 891 | 16.52 ms | 2.47 |

Every PR run is above every main run: +6.2% against the median of the 8 main runs, with the same acceptance. That fits the per-step stream sync you saw in the profile.

**Throughput, GB300.** We used the same GB300 setup without deterministic mode (`--disable-radix-cache`, default attention backend) and the same image bench (seeds 1–3, warm-up first). The runs were A-B-B-A on one node, in a single allocation. "A" is this PR's tree with only `forward_batch_info.py` swapped back to main's version.

| arm | out tok/s (seeds 1–3) | median TPOT |
|---|---|---:|
| main | 861 / 857 / 888 | 17.46 / 18.03 / 16.82 ms |
| this PR | 997 / 1013 / 1014 | 14.92 / 14.97 / 14.85 ms |
| this PR | 1008 / 998 / 970 | 14.67 / 15.10 / 14.98 ms |
| main | 889 / 887 / 881 | 17.18 / 17.47 / 16.90 ms |

That is a median of 1003 vs 884 tok/s (+13.5%) and a median TPOT of 14.95 vs 17.32 ms (−14%), with accept length 2.42–2.44 in every run. The gain is larger here than in the TP2 RTX setup above. We did not isolate why (different host CPU, TP and checkpoint), but it is consistent with the multi-ms stalls in your profile.

Thanks for the thorough end-to-end validation — and especially the A-B-B-A ablation that isolates`forward_batch_info.py` . That pins the gain to exactly the change in this PR, which is the strongest possible evidence.

The numbers line up with what I measured locally: the per-step pinning/sync removal is the whole effect, and accept length staying at 2.42–2.44 across every run confirms this is purely transfer-latency removal with no effect on speculation quality.

On the TP2 (+6.2%) vs GB300 (+13.5%) gap — my guess is that TP2 dilutes the gain: per-step tensor-parallel communication is a larger, fixed fraction of step latency, so the CPU-side stall is relatively smaller. GB300 TP1 has no TP sync, so the removed stall is a bigger share of each step (host CPU / checkpoint differences may also contribute, as you noted). 

I'll fold these numbers into the PR description so the verification is visible to reviewers. Thanks again!

@hnyls2002 @merrymercy — could one of you take a look when you have a chance?

This is a small, focused change: in`compute_spec_mrope_positions` (`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py` ), stage the MRoPE delta through a pinned host buffer before the H2D copy, avoiding the blocking pageable copy that PyTorch syncs the stream on. This path runs on every speculative-decode step with multimodal requests, and the sync was turning an 8-byte copy into a multi-ms stall per step.

Summary of validation:

- Numerically identical to the original across batch sizes 1/2/5/17/64 and mixed single/multi-step compositions; existing`test_spec_mrope_positions_graph` passes unmodified.
- Host-side call time stays ~0.1 ms vs ~260 ms for the original blocking copy under real GPU load (stream no longer drained).
- Third-party end-to-end on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next / NEXTN MTP (by @esarafian): identical outputs vs main, and +13.5% throughput / −14% median TPOT on GB300 (A-B-B-A ablation isolating this file), +6.2% on RTX PRO 6000 TP2, accept length unchanged.
Happy to address any feedback. Thanks!
